findings.title: Call to undefined no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() will not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method with that name introduced by this PR is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm (line 160), and neither UsernameForm nor AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator defines a no-argument overload. As written the services module fails to compile (cannot find symbol). The guard should most likely call `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, or a no-arg overload must be added to the superclass.

findings.title: Passkeys data no longer populated on the initial (user not yet selected) login page
findings.body: The condition that drives `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` was inverted: previously it ran inside the `context.getUser() == null` branch (initial page), now it runs outside the branch and only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which requires a non-null user (line 161). Consequently the conditional-passkeys/WebAuthn attributes (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, etc.) are no longer set on the first page rendered before a username is entered. The same inversion was applied to the `challenge(error, field)` override (line 137). This regresses first-page passkey login: existing tests that are unchanged by this PR still assert the `//form[@id='webauth']` element is present and click the WebAuthn 'Authenticate' button on the very first page (e.g. PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey and passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey, and PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey). Unless a separate passkeys execution renders that page, those flows will fail. Conditional UI is specifically meant to work before a user is identified, so gating on `user != null` is suspect.

findings.title: Unused import of NoSuchElementException after assertions were replaced
findings.body: The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` checks in passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., notNullValue())`, but `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is still imported (line 51) and no longer referenced anywhere in the file (`Assert` is still used at line 134). Keycloak's build enforces checkstyle UnusedImports, so this will fail the build/verify of the testsuite module.
